1.q: וַ⁠יְהִי֩ דְבַר יְהוָ֨ה אֵלַ֜⁠י בַּ⁠שָּׁנָ֤ה הַ⁠תְּשִׁיעִית֙
1.note: Ezekiel is using the phrase translated as **And the word of Yahweh was to me in the ninth year** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated this expression in 20:2.

2.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02).

Yahweh is using **the name of the day** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the date.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the date]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the king of Babylon had **pressed against** Jerusalem with his body. It means that the king has surrounded the city with his army and has begun to attack it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The king of Babylon has surrounded Jerusalem with his army and begun to attack it]

3.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel were a **house**, that is, a family. It means that they are a single group of people who are related to one another, and this group is characterized by **rebellion**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the rebellious people of Israel]

3.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֑ה שְׁפֹ֤ת הַ⁠סִּיר֙ שְׁפֹ֔ת
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and you shall tell them that the Lord Yahweh says that they should set on the pot, set it on]

3.q: שְׁפֹ֤ת הַ⁠סִּיר֙ שְׁפֹ֔ת וְ⁠גַם יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖⁠וֹ מָֽיִם
3.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if Jerusalem were a cooking **pot** that someone was setting on a fire and filling with **water**. It means that the people inside Jerusalem are about to suffer greatly during the Babylonian siege, like food that is being cooked in a pot over a fire. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Get ready to besiege Jerusalem, get ready, and also prepare to make its people suffer greatly]

4.q: אֱסֹ֤ף נְתָחֶ֨י⁠הָ֙ אֵלֶ֔י⁠הָ כָּל נֵ֥תַח ט֖וֹב יָרֵ֣ךְ וְ⁠כָתֵ֑ף
4.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Jerusalem were **pieces** of meat that someone was putting into a pot, including **every good piece** such as the **thigh and shoulder**. It means that all the people, including the most important people, will be gathered inside Jerusalem when Yahweh judges the city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Gather the people of Jerusalem like pieces of meat into the pot, every important person like a good piece of thigh and shoulder]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **the choicest of bones** after the command to **fill** the pot. Alternate translation: [fill it with the choicest of bones]

5.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the leading people of Jerusalem were **the choicest of the flock**, that is, the best sheep. It means that Yahweh’s judgment will include even the most important people in the city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [take the most important people of the city, who are like the best sheep of the flock]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.

6.note: Yahweh is using **Woe** as a common expression of the culture to mean “How terrible it will be for.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Disaster will come upon the city of bloods]

Here, **bloods** represents “murders.” Yahweh is describing Jerusalem as a city where people have murdered many others. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the city of many murders]

6.q: סִ֚יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֶלְאָתָ֣⁠ה בָ֔⁠הּ וְ⁠חֶ֨לְאָתָ֔⁠הּ לֹ֥א יָצְאָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑⁠נָּה
6.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if Jerusalem were a **pot** that has **rust** in it that has **not gone out from it**. It means that the people of Jerusalem are full of wickedness that they have not gotten rid of. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the city whose people are full of wickedness, but they have not gotten rid of their wickedness]

Yahweh is using **To its pieces, to its pieces** as a common expression of the culture to mean “piece by piece” or “one piece at a time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Bring it out piece by piece]

Yahweh is using **a lot has not fallen on it** as a common expression of the culture to mean “no one has cast lots to choose any of it.” This indicates that no pieces will be chosen to be spared; all of them will be taken out. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [no one has chosen any piece to be spared]

7.note: Here, **her blood** represents “the murders that the people of Jerusalem committed.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [For the blood from the murders she committed is in her midst]

The pronoun **her** refers to Jerusalem. In the previous verse, Yahweh spoke of the city as a pot, but here he speaks of the city as if it were a woman. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [For the blood that Jerusalem shed is in the middle of the city]

7.q: עַל צְחִ֥יחַ סֶ֖לַע שָׂמָ֑תְ⁠הוּ לֹ֤א שְׁפָכַ֨תְ⁠הוּ֙ עַל הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ לְ⁠כַסּ֥וֹת עָלָ֖י⁠ו עָפָֽר
7.note: The implication is that the people of Jerusalem did not follow the custom of covering the blood of someone who had been killed with **dust**, which showed respect for life. Instead, they left the blood of the people they had murdered exposed for everyone to see, because they were not ashamed of what they had done. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on the bare surface of a rock she placed it, openly, for everyone to see, because she was not ashamed. She did not pour it on the ground to cover over it with dust, as people did to show respect for life]

8.q: לְ⁠הַעֲל֤וֹת חֵמָה֙ לִ⁠נְקֹ֣ם נָקָ֔ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת דָּמָ֖⁠הּ עַל צְחִ֣יחַ סָ֑לַע
8.note: Here, **To** marks **make heat ascend, to avenge vengeance** as the goal or purpose of **I have put her blood on the bare surface of a rock**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

Yahweh is using **To make heat ascend** as a common expression of the culture to mean “To cause my anger to rise.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [To stir up my anger]

8.q: נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת דָּמָ֖⁠הּ עַל צְחִ֣יחַ סָ֑לַע לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֖י הִכָּסֽוֹת
8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if he had **put her blood on the bare surface of a rock** where no one would cover it. It means that Yahweh has made sure that the guilt of the people of Jerusalem for their murders remains plainly visible, so that he will punish them for it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have made sure that her guilt for murder remains plainly visible to everyone]

The expression **without it being covered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh means that no one will cover the blood. Alternate translation: [without anyone covering it]

9.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **will grow** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he himself will act against the city. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [Also I myself will grow the pile]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if he were going to make a larger **pile** of firewood under the pot. It means that he will make his punishment of Jerusalem more severe. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will punish her more severely]

The implication is that **the pile** is a pile of wood under the pot. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I will grow the pile of wood under the pot]
See how you translated the similar expression in 24:6.

10.q: הַרְבֵּ֤ה הָ⁠עֵצִים֙ הַדְלֵ֣ק הָ⁠אֵ֔שׁ הָתֵ֖ם הַ⁠בָּשָׂ֑ר
10.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if he were commanding someone to cook the meat in the pot by adding more **wood**, kindling **the fire**, and **finishing the flesh**. It means that Yahweh will completely destroy Jerusalem and its people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Destroy the city completely, like someone who adds much wood and kindles the fire, finishing the flesh]

Yahweh is using **mixing the spice mixture** as a common expression of the culture to mean “adding spices to the meat.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and adding spices to the meat]

The expression **let them be burned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and burn the bones]

11.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the sins of the people of Jerusalem were **uncleanness** and **rot** inside a pot that a hot fire would remove. It means that Yahweh will remove the sin from the city by destroying it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the sins of its people are melted away inside it; its wickedness comes to an end]

The expression **is poured** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to state what does the action, the context indicates that the heat of the fire does it. Alternate translation: [and the heat melts its uncleanness in its midst]

12.note: Yahweh is using **toil, it has wearied** as a common expression of the culture to mean “All the efforts to clean it have been useless.” Alternatively, Yahweh may be saying that the city has worn itself out with its evil deeds. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All the efforts to clean it have been useless]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **abundance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [its abundant rot]

With the words **into a fire, its rust**, Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of disgust. He means that the pot with its rust should be thrown into the fire. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [into a fire with it, rust and all]

13.note: If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **uncleanness** and **obscenity**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [You are unclean because you have acted obscenely]

13.q: יַ֤עַן טִֽהַרְתִּי⁠ךְ֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א טָהַ֔רְתְּ מִ⁠טֻּמְאָתֵ⁠ךְ֙ לֹ֣א תִטְהֲרִי ע֔וֹד
13.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Jerusalem were dirty and he had tried to wash them so that they would be **clean**. It means that Yahweh tried to stop the people from sinning so that they would be acceptable to him, but they continued to sin. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Because I tried to stop you from sinning so that you would be acceptable to me, but you kept on sinning, you will not be acceptable to me again]
The word **you** is singular here because it refers to the city of Jerusalem. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his anger, which he calls his **heat**, were something that he could lay on a person. It means that he will punish the people of Jerusalem because he is angry with them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [until I have punished you because of my anger]

14.note: The pronoun **It** refers to the punishment that Yahweh has announced. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The punishment is coming, and I will carry it out]

14.q: לֹֽא אֶפְרַ֥ע וְ⁠לֹא אָח֖וּס וְ⁠לֹ֣א אֶנָּחֵ֑ם
14.note: The phrases **I will not refrain**, **I will not have pity**, and **I will not relent** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three phrases together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [I will certainly not show you any mercy]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the behavior of the people of Jerusalem were **ways**, that is, paths along which they walked. It means the way that they have lived and the things that they have done. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [According to how you have behaved and according to what you have done]

Here Yahweh is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you have been judged]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **declaration**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:15.

15.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [6:1](ta:06).

16.note: Yahweh is using **behold me—taking from you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am about to take from you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to take from you]

Here, **the delight of your eyes** represents “the one whom you delight to look at.” Verse 18 shows that Yahweh is referring to Ezekiel’s wife. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your beloved wife]

16.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א תִסְפֹּד֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּ֔ה וְ⁠ל֥וֹא תָב֖וֹא דִּמְעָתֶֽ⁠ךָ
16.note: The phrases **you shall not mourn**, **you shall not weep**, and **your tears shall not come** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the three phrases together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [But you must not grieve at all]

16.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א תִסְפֹּד֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּ֔ה וְ⁠ל֥וֹא תָב֖וֹא דִּמְעָתֶֽ⁠ךָ
16.note: Yahweh is using future statements to give instructions or commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words using a command or instruction form. Alternate translation: [But do not mourn, and do not weep, and do not let your tears come]

17.note: The words **Groan** and **be silent** express a single idea. The second word tells more about the first: Ezekiel should groan quietly. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [Groan silently]

17.q: פְאֵֽרְ⁠ךָ֙ חֲב֣וֹשׁ עָלֶ֔י⁠ךָ וּ⁠נְעָלֶ֖י⁠ךָ תָּשִׂ֣ים בְּ⁠רַגְלֶ֑י⁠ךָ
17.note: Wearing a turban and sandals as usual would be a symbolic action by which Ezekiel showed that he was not mourning, because people who mourned would normally take these off. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Bind your turban on yourself, and your sandals you shall put on your feet, as usual, to show that you are not mourning]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **your sandals** after the command to put them on. Alternate translation: [and you shall put your sandals on your feet]

Covering the lower part of the face was a symbolic action by which people in this culture showed that they were mourning. By not doing this, Ezekiel would show that he was not mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and you shall not cover over your mustache as people do to show that they are mourning]

Yahweh is using **the bread of men** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the food that people bring to someone who is mourning.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you shall not eat the food that people bring to mourners]

18.note: The expression **I was commanded** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to state who did the action, Ezekiel implies that Yahweh did it. Alternate translation: [just as Yahweh had commanded me]

19.q: הֲ⁠לֹֽא תַגִּ֥יד לָ֨⁠נוּ֙ מָה אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֔⁠נוּ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה
19.note: The people are using the question form to urge Ezekiel to explain what he is doing. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Please declare to us what these things that you are doing mean for us!]

19.q: הֲ⁠לֹֽא תַגִּ֥יד לָ֨⁠נוּ֙ מָה אֵ֣לֶּה לָּ֔⁠נוּ
19.note: By **us**, the people mean themselves but not Ezekiel, to whom they are speaking, so use the exclusive form of that word in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

20.q: וָ⁠אֹמַ֖ר אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֑ם דְּבַ֨ר יְהוָ֔ה הָיָ֥ה אֵלַ֖⁠י לֵ⁠אמֹֽר
20.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And I told them that the word of Yahweh had come to me, telling me to say this]

21.q: אֱמֹ֣ר לְ⁠בֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִה֒ הִנְ⁠נִ֨י מְחַלֵּ֤ל אֶת מִקְדָּשִׁ⁠י֙
21.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Say to the house of Israel that the Lord Yahweh says that he is about to profane his sanctuary]

Yahweh is using **Behold me—profaning** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am about to profane.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to profane my sanctuary]

21.q: אֶת מִקְדָּשִׁ⁠י֙ גְּא֣וֹן עֻזְּ⁠כֶ֔ם מַחְמַ֥ד עֵֽינֵי⁠כֶ֖ם וּ⁠מַחְמַ֣ל נַפְשְׁ⁠כֶ֑ם
21.note: Yahweh is not distinguishing this **sanctuary** from another sanctuary that is not **the pride of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and the longing of your soul**. Yahweh is reminding the people about how much they valued the temple. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [my sanctuary, which you are so proud of, which you delight to look at, and which you long for]

21.q: גְּא֣וֹן עֻזְּ⁠כֶ֔ם מַחְמַ֥ד עֵֽינֵי⁠כֶ֖ם וּ⁠מַחְמַ֣ל נַפְשְׁ⁠כֶ֑ם
21.note: Here, **the pride of your strength**, **the desire of your eyes**, and **the longing of your soul** represent the temple by the feelings that it caused in the people. They mean that the people were proud of the temple because they thought it made them strong, that they delighted to look at it, and that they loved it deeply. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the building that you are proud of because you think it makes you strong, that you delight to look at, and that you love deeply]

Yahweh is using **will fall by the sword** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will be killed in battle.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will be killed in battle]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03).

22.note: The word **you** is plural here because Ezekiel is addressing the people of Israel, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

22.q: עַל שָׂפָם֙ לֹ֣א תַעְט֔וּ וְ⁠לֶ֥חֶם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ
22.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the **mustache** and **the bread of men** after the verbs **cover** and **eat**. Alternate translation: [You will not cover over your mustache, and you will not eat the bread of men]

23.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people would **rot** like spoiled food. It means that they will waste away because of the punishment they receive for their sins. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But you will become weaker and weaker as you are punished for your iniquities]

Here the masculine terms **man** and **brother** have a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [and you will groan, each person to his or her fellow Israelite]

Yahweh is using **a man to his brother** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to one another.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [each of you with the others]

24.note: Ezekiel is repeating what Yahweh told him to say to the people, so he speaks of himself in the third person as **Ezekiel**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [And I, Ezekiel, will be for you as a sign]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Ezekiel were a **sign**. It means that what Ezekiel does will show the people what is going to happen to them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And what Ezekiel does will show you what is going to happen to you]

The pronoun **it** refers to the punishment that Yahweh has said he will bring on Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [When this punishment comes, then you will know]

25.q: הֲ⁠ל֗וֹא בְּ⁠י֨וֹם קַחְתִּ֤⁠י מֵ⁠הֶם֙ אֶת מָ֣עוּזָּ֔⁠ם
25.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that what he is saying will certainly happen. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [it will certainly be so on the day of my taking from them their stronghold]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the temple were the people’s **stronghold**, a fortress that protected them. It means that the people trusted that the temple would keep them safe. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the temple that they trusted to keep them safe]

If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **joy** and **splendor**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [what made them rejoice because it was so splendid]

Yahweh is using **the lifting up of their soul** as a common expression of the culture to mean “what they long for.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly.
